canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop and evaluate a MedGemma-based multimodal framework for prostate cancer segmentation, Gleason grade group classification, survival prediction, and structured clinical rationale generation.

The framework used modality-specific MRI, ultrasound, and WSI encoders; hierarchical multiple-instance learning for WSI; modality availability masks; gated cross-attention; and dedicated segmentation, grading, survival, and rationale outputs.

Unavailable modalities were represented by learned null tokens and masked from task-specific losses, allowing the same backbone to support MRI-only, MRI+US, MRI+WSI, WSI-only, or full trimodal inputs without imputing nonexistent data.
The reported implementation used the MedGemma 4B multimodal backbone, MedSigLIP-derived radiology features, a hierarchical WSI MIL encoder, modality adapters, and task-specific heads.
WSI tissue was tiled at 20× magnification into 256×256-pixel patches with 50% overlap; patches were retained when at least 60% of their area was tissue.

source_anchor.paragraph: WSI Patch Level Supervision and MIL Integration

canonical_statement: Typical WSI MIL bags contained 128-256 patches during training and up to the top 512 attention-ranked patches during inference.

source_anchor.paragraph: WSI Patch Level Supervision and MIL Integration

canonical_statement: When only slide-level WSI labels were available, slide loss supervised the aggregate representation and attention maps were treated as weak localization rather than pixel-level ground truth.

source_anchor.paragraph: WSI Patch Level Supervision and MIL Integration

canonical_statement: MRI+US fusion was used only when tracked biopsy data, prostate-surface registration, or anatomical landmarks supplied correspondence; target gland masks were reserved for evaluation rather than used as validation or test inputs.

source_anchor.paragraph: Rationale for Cross-Modal Fusion and Spatial Correspondence

canonical_statement: In registered MRI+US analyses, ultrasound was intended to contribute procedural-space information such as gland boundary geometry, deformation state, echotexture, and target coordinates rather than microscopic pathology.

source_anchor.paragraph: Rationale for Cross-Modal Fusion and Spatial Correspondence

canonical_statement: MRI+WSI fusion was restricted to datasets with slice-level MRI-to-histology correspondence and cancer annotations; unregistered WSI was used for WSI-centered grading or survival rather than voxel-level MRI segmentation.

source_anchor.paragraph: Rationale for Cross-Modal Fusion and Spatial Correspondence

canonical_statement: Cross-modal fusion used gated cross-attention over aligned or semantically compatible token sets, with spatial correspondence terms included when available and corresponding task losses masked when spatial correspondence was absent.

source_anchor.paragraph: Rationale for Cross-Modal Fusion and Spatial Correspondence

canonical_statement: Supervised training activated only the classification, segmentation, survival, alignment, and patch losses supported by the labels in each task-specific batch.

Optimization proceeded through supervised task training, validation-stage alignment and output calibration, and reinforcement learning for rationale generation with visual encoders and task heads frozen during the third stage.

source_anchor.paragraph: Loss Functions and Stage-Wise Optimization; Algorithm 1

canonical_statement: The rationale reward combined final-answer correctness, factuality, grounding, cross-output consistency, and a penalty for excessive length.

source_anchor.paragraph: Reinforcement Learning for Structured Clinical Rationale Optimization

canonical_statement: During reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, only decoder adapters were updated; segmentation and survival heads were not updated.

source_anchor.paragraph: Reinforcement Learning for Structured Clinical Rationale Optimization

canonical_statement: Machine outputs were separated from explanatory text: task heads produced segmentation masks, grade outputs, and survival risk scores, while the decoder produced a structured rationale containing modality observations, consistency, differential considerations, uncertainty, and a conclusion.

source_anchor.paragraph: Model Input/Output Structure and Rationale Format

canonical_statement: The rationale audit used 40 stratified model-generated rationales, two independent clinical reviewers, 80 rater-case assessments, and 160 structured statements for unsupported-assertion counting.
Grounding perturbation compared masking the image region or WSI tiles cited by a rationale with masking a random control region of comparable size.

The public resources were treated as task-specific datasets rather than one fully paired MRI+US+WSI cohort, and MedGemma rows represented the same architectural family with dataset-specific modality masks, heads, and splits.

MRI preprocessing used T2-weighted imaging as the spatial reference when available, registered ADC and high-b-value DWI to T2W, and applied bias correction, resampling, prostate-centered cropping, z-score normalization, and robust-percentile clipping.
TRUS preprocessing used light denoising, robust-percentile clipping, per-volume normalization, and resampling to MRI coordinates when tracked biopsy or registration fields were available.
WSI stain normalization was fitted on the training set only; tissue masking preceded tiling, insufficient-tissue patches were discarded, and artifact patches were excluded or down-weighted.
Experiments used one node with four NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, mixed precision, distributed decoder sharding, AdamW optimization, cosine decay, and 10% warmup.
RL fine-tuning used group size 8, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, a maximum of 512 rationale tokens, and AdamW with learning rate 10^-5.

All splits were patient-level; all slides from one TCGA-PRAD patient remained in one split, and published-reference rows were treated as descriptive context rather than paired statistical comparisons.

source_anchor.paragraph: Benchmarking, Source Labels and Statistical Testing

canonical_statement: Confidence intervals used patient-level resampling; paired tests were limited to prespecified same-case contrasts with paired predictions, and Holm adjustment was applied only to predefined primary comparisons generated in the study.

source_anchor.paragraph: Benchmarking, Source Labels and Statistical Testing

canonical_statement: The survival endpoint was progression-free interval as defined in TCGA-CDR, using the endpoint file for event status, time origin, follow-up, and censoring.

canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the matched MRI+US perturbation contrasts as evidence that aligned ultrasound contributed boundary and registration information rather than an independent histopathologic signal.
The authors concluded that the framework provides a structured approach to multimodal prostate cancer modeling while making data-pairing assumptions explicit.

The authors identified the framework's most appropriate current use as research on registered radiology-pathology fusion, WSI-centered grading, and WSI-based survival discrimination rather than routine clinical deployment.
A definitive trimodal same-patient evaluation was not possible because no cohort contained matched MRI, ultrasound, WSI, grade labels, segmentation masks, and survival follow-up.
Published comparator rows could not support definitive superiority claims because patient-level predictions, preprocessing, and splits were not shared.
WSI localization through MIL attention was not equivalent to pixel-level pathology segmentation.
The study did not provide the runtime, calibration, external validation, model compression, or prospective clinical workflow evidence needed for deployment assessment.

The rationale audit was explicitly limited to output-level factuality, grounding, and consistency and did not establish that generated rationales were causally faithful to the model's hidden reasoning.
The study used de-identified public datasets, introduced no new human-subject data collection, and included no non-public institutional data.

The authors stated that all datasets were publicly accessible and that the reproducibility package versioned derived splits, table-specific prediction files, and the TCGA survival endpoint file.

The authors reported an anonymized code repository containing source code, preprocessing configurations, experiment configurations, evaluation scripts, prediction files, and task-specific adapter checkpoints where permitted.
